The circuit shown in figure must provide a voltage gain of -6, with CS serving as a low impedance at
the frequencies of interest. Assuming a power budget of 2 mW and an input impedance of 20 kΩ,
design the circuit such that M1 operates 200 mV away from the triode region. Assume µnCox = 200
µA/V2, λ=0, and VTH=0.4V, ignore capacitances.

An NMOS device carries 1 mA with VGS− VTH = 0.6 V and 1.6 mA with VGS − VTH = 0.8 V. If the
device operates in the triode region, calculate VDS and W/L.

Design an NMOS cascode for an output impedance of 500 kΩ and a current of 0.5 mA. Assume M1
and M2 are identical, µnCox = 200 µA/V2 and λ = 0.1V−1.

Design an NMOS differential pair for a voltage gain of 5 and a power budget of 2 mW subject to the
condition that the stage following the differential pair requires an input CM (common mode) level of
at least 1.6 V. Assume µnCox = 100 µA/V2, λ = 0, and VDD = 1.8V.

Figure shows an arrangement where M1 and M2 serve as current sources for circuits 1 and 2.
Design the circuit for a power budget of 3 mW.

Assume µnCox = 200 µA/V2, λ = 0, and VTH = 0.4V. For a drain current of 1 mA. If W/L = 20/0.18.
For the circuit shown, compute R1 and R2 such that the input impedance is at least 20KΩ.

Design the circuit shown below with a voltage gain of -20, power budget of 1 mW and VDD = 1.8 V.
Assume M1 operates at the edge of saturation if the input common-mode level is 1V. Also, µnCox =
2µpCox = 100 µA/V2, VTH,n = 0.5 V, VTH,p = -0.4 V, λn = 0.5V-1, λp = 0.1 V-1.

For the amplifier shown, gm = (100Ω)-1, λ = 0, RD = 2KΩ, RS = 200Ω, Cin = 1µF, and CL = 50nF.
Neglecting the MOSFET capacitance, sketch the frequency response of the amplifier indicating the
pole frequencies.

For the circuit shown below, find the poles at low frequencies. Also, sketch its low frequency
response. Assume λ = 0.

For the circuit shown, determine the input and output poles at high frequencies for λ= 0. Sketch the
frequency response.
Determine the polarity of feedback in the circuit shown below.

For the circuit shown below, obtain the expressions for gain and frequency of oscillation. Also,
extend the result for Hartley and Colpitts's oscillator.

Determine the closed-loop gain, closed-loop input impedance, and closed-loop output impedance
for the circuit shown below. Consider I/O effects (Loading Effect). Assume λ=0 for both M1 and M2.

Obtain an expression for % efficiency of Class A power amplifier and find its maximum value, also
draw the circuit diagram.

For the circuit shown below, obtain the expressions for gain and the frequency of oscillation. Also,
find the frequency of oscillation for R=100KΩ and C=0.1µF.

Explain the basic block diagram of an operational amplifier with a neat diagram and plot its transfer
characteristics. Also, explain the characteristics of an ideal op-amp with proper definitions.

Characterize each of the following amplifiers by feedback type. As well for each, find β in terms of
the labelled components. In all cases, assume that the op-amp is ideal.

Design the phase shift oscillator of Figure shown below for a frequency of 10 MHz, assuming an
ideal opamp. Assume C1 =C2 =C3 = 1nF.

Explain the concept of Voltage-Voltage feedback with a neat diagram and derive the expressions for
effective input impedance, output impedance, and gain.

Design the MOS differential amplifier shown in figure, for operating overdrive voltage of 0.25 V and
to provide a transconductance of 1mA/V. Consider VTH =0.5V and µnCox =100 µA/V2.

A current-mirror-loaded NMOS differential pair has the following parameters: µnCox = 100 µA/V²,
µpCox = 50 µA/V², (W/L)n = 40/0.5, (W/L)p = 80/0.5, ISS = 0.8 mA, λn = 0.05 V-1, and λp = 0.1 V-1.
Calculate
(a). Transconductance gm of input transistors Q1 and Q2.
(b). Output resistance ro2 and ro4
(c). Differential gain Ad

A high-pass active filter with gain is implemented as shown in figure. The filter has the following
measured characteristics:
• At f = 50 Hz: |H| = 0.5 V/V, ∠H = +45°
• At f = 10 kHz: |H| = 12 V/V, ∠H = +5°
(a) Analyze the circuit to determine the 3-dB cutoff frequency (f₀) and high-frequency gain (H₀).
(b) If R₁ = 47 kΩ and C = 68 nF, calculate R₂ and verify whether still the circuit works as HPF for the
H₀ and f₀ obtained in the part (a). If not suggest the values changes in the C and R2 components.

Using standard 5% resistor values, design a two stage circuit that produces the output voltage V₀ =
8V₁ + 12V₂ - 4V₃. Provide the complete circuit diagram and a detailed step-by-step solution justifying
your component choices. The input impedance if 1st stage is 10 kΩ. Hint: You can use unity gain
inverting amplifier and the 1st stage with followed by difference amplifier in the 2nd stage.

What is an Opamp window detector? Explain the working of it with relevant circuit diagram and its
voltage transfer characteristics.

The standard astable multivibrator circuit using a 555 timer cannot achieve a duty cycle of exactly
50%. Propose and explain a circuit (with potentiometer) modification to achieve i) duty cycle less
than 50% ii) duty cycle more than 50%

Design a simple automatic light control system using a 555 timer for a staircase. When a person
presses a push button, a light bulb should turn ON and remain ON for 2 minutes, after which it
should automatically turn OFF. The system uses a 9V battery.

Explain the advantages of using a current-mirror-loaded differential amplifier over a traditional
resistor loaded differential pair for single-ended output applications. Derive the differential voltage
gain for the current-mirror-loaded configuration.
-----End-----

RDID = 1 V, determine the required value of W/L. Assume the capacitors are very large, RG =
10KΩ, µnCox = 200 µA/V2, λ=0, and VTH=0.4V.
Using a small signal model, calculate the voltage gain for the circuit shown below. Consider λ=0.

Using the small signal model, compute the output resistance of the circuits depicted below. Assume
all the transistors operate in saturation. Consider λ≠0.

Design the MOS differential amplifier shown below to operate at an overdrive voltage of 0.25 V and
to provide a transconductance of 1mA/V. Consider VTH =0.5V and µnCox =100 µA/V2.

An integrated circuit employs the source follower and the common-source stage, as shown in the
figure below. Design a current mirror that produces I1 and I2 from a 0.3mA reference. Assume λ=0.

Consider the circuit shown below. Calculate the maximum transconductance that M1 can provide
(without going into the triode region). Assume µnCox = 200 µA/V2 , λ=0, and VTH=0.4V.

Determine the expression of single-ended differential voltage gain for the circuit shown below.
Assume perfect symmetry and λ ≠ 0.

For the amplifier shown, determine the pole frequencies. Ignore the parasitic capacitance of the
MOSFET and consider λ=0.

In the circuit shown below, RD = 1KΩ and CL = 1pF. Neglecting channel-length modulation and
other capacitances. Determine the frequency at which the gain falls by 10%.

Identify all the capacitance and reduce the source follower circuit shown to compute the poles.
Assume λ=0.
Determine the polarity of the feedback of the circuit and justify the same.

Explain the working principle of the Colpitts Oscillator with a neat circuit diagram. Also, obtain an
expression for frequency of oscillation and find the frequency of oscillation for L1 = 2mH and C1 =
C2 = 10µF.

Analyze the circuit shown where the output current delivered to a laser is regulated by negative
feedback taking loading effect of feedback into account. Compute the closed-loop gain and I/O
impedances, considering λ=0 and model the laser as resistance RL.
Explain the working principle of Class - B power amplifier with a neat circuit diagram.

Explain the working principle of RC phase shift oscillator with a neat circuit diagram and relevant
expressions. Also, find the frequency of oscillation for capacitance of 0.01µF and resistance of
10KΩ.

Determine the region of operation of M1 in each circuit shown in the Figure below. Assume VTH =
0.4V.

An NMOS device operating in saturation with λ = 0 must provide a transconductance of 1/(50Ω).
Assume µnCox = 100 µA/V²
(a) Determine W/L if ID = 0.5 mA.
(b) Determine W/L if VGS - VTH = 0.5V.
(c) Determine ID if VGS - VTH = 0.5V.

Explain the basic block diagram of an operational amplifier with a neat diagram and plot its transfer
characteristics. Also, explain the characteristics of an ideal op-amp with proper definitions.

Calculate the gain with and without feedback for an FET amplifier as shown below for circuit values
R1 = 800 kΩ, R2 = 200 Ω, Ro = 40 kΩ, RD = 8 kΩ, and gm = 5000 µS.

Design the Wein bridge oscillator of Figure shown below for a frequency of 10 MHz, assuming an
ideal opamp. Assume C1 =C2 = 1 nF.

Explain the concept of Voltage-Current feedback with a neat diagram and derive the expressions for
effective input impedance, output impedance, and gain.

Consider the circuit of figure, where a common-source stage (M1 and RD1) is followed by a
common-gate stage (M2 and RD2).
(a) Writing Vout/Vin = (Vx/Vin)(Vout/Vx) and assuming λ = 0, compute the overall voltage gain.
(b) Simplify the result obtained in (a) if RD1 → ∞. Explain why this result is to be expected.

Design the phase shift oscillator as shown in the figure for a frequency of 4 MHz with C1 =C2 =C3 =
1nF. Assume ideal op-amp behavior for the design. Find R1 = R2 = R3 and 5% feedback resistors
to meet the oscillation gain requirement.

A MOS differential pair has µnCox = 100 µA/V², W/L = 20/0.18, VTH = 0.5 V, VDD = VSS = 1.5 V, RD
= 2.5 kΩ, and ISS = 0.4 mA. The current source requires minimum 0.4 V to operate properly.
(a) Calculate the equilibrium overdrive voltage and VGS for each transistor.
(b) For VCM = 0 V, find VS, ID1, ID2, VD1, and VD2.
(c) Determine the highest permitted value of VCM.

Design a first-order active low-pass filter (shown in figure) with gain using an op-amp that meets the
following specifications: DC gain (H₀) = 26 dB, 3-dB cutoff frequency (f₀) = 2.5 kHz, Input resistance
= 20 kΩ
(a) Calculate the required component values (R₁, R₂, and C).
(b) Determine the actual gain magnitude and phase angle at frequency f = 10 kHz.

Using standard 5% resistor values, design a two-stage circuit that produces the output voltage V₀ =
5V₁ + 10V₂ - 2V₃. Provide the complete circuit diagram and a detailed step-by-step solution
justifying your component choices. The input impedance for the first stage inputs should be 22 kΩ.

What are the limitations of standard half-wave precision rectifier. Explain the improved/modified
version of it with circuit diagram input and out waveform.

Show the standard configuration for the astable multivibrator using the 555 timer with external
components, that cannot achieve exactly 50% duty cycle. Evaluate this limitation by deriving the
duty cycle expression.Explain why 50% duty cycle cannot be achieved and propose the circuit
modifications to overcome this limitation.

Design a monostable multivibrator using an IC 555 timer that produces a positive output pulse with
a duration of 200 ms. Select a capacitor value of 0.2 µF, and calculate the required resistance.
Draw the final (a) circuit diagram, (b) voltage across the capacitor, (c) trigger input and (d) output
waveform.

For the MOS differential pair shown in the figure, a common-mode input VCM i.e., a small
differential input signal ΔV is applied such that Vin1 = VCM + ΔV and Vin2 = VCM - ΔV.
Derive an expression for the small-signal differential voltage gain, AV = (ΔVx - ΔVy) / (2ΔV). Show
that this gain is similar to that of a common-source stage.
-----End-----
